chapters.name: Survival
chapters.role: First 2 weeks: cravings, triggers, get through each day

days.title: Day 1: You quit
days.intro: Today is the hardest day to start and the most important one. You do not need willpower for ninety days right now. You need it for the next ten minutes, then the ten after that.

tasks.title: Remove every cigarette and lighter
tasks.text: Go through your home, car, bag and desk and throw away every cigarette, lighter and ashtray you own. Do not save one for emergencies.

tasks.title: Do your first craving reset
tasks.text: Open the craving tool once now, even if you do not feel a craving yet, so you know exactly where it is when you need it.

days.title: Day 2: The hardest part is starting
days.intro: Nicotine is mostly out of your blood by now, which is why today can feel rough. That is your body healing, not your body failing.

tasks.title: Know what is happening in your body
tasks.text: Your heart rate and blood pressure are already dropping back toward normal. Carbon monoxide levels in your blood have dropped and oxygen is reaching your muscles and organs better than two days ago.

tasks.title: Tell one person you trust
tasks.text: Message or call one person and tell them you quit smoking yesterday. Saying it out loud to someone makes it real and gives you one more reason to follow through.

days.title: Day 3: Peak craving day
days.intro: Nicotine withdrawal symptoms are usually strongest around day 3. This is the peak, not the new normal. It gets easier from here.

tasks.title: Ride out one craving with the tool
tasks.text: Next time a craving hits, open the craving tool instead of fighting it in your head. Let it guide you through it.

tasks.title: Write down today's hardest moment
tasks.text: In one or two sentences, write what time of day was hardest today and what you were doing right before the craving hit.

days.title: Day 4: Naming your triggers
days.intro: Cravings rarely come out of nowhere. They are usually attached to a place, a feeling, or a habit. Today you start spotting yours.

tasks.title: List your top three triggers
tasks.text: Write down the three moments that make you want a cigarette the most right now, for example morning coffee, after meals, or stress at work.

tasks.title: Change one small routine
tasks.text: Pick one trigger from your list and change something physical about it today, like drinking your coffee in a different spot or taking a different route on your break.

tasks.title: See your money saved so far
tasks.text: Check your stats tab and look at how much money you have already kept in your pocket since day one.

days.title: Day 5: Your hands need a job
days.intro: A lot of the urge to smoke is physical, not just mental. Your hands and mouth are used to having something to do.

tasks.title: Pick a hand stand in
tasks.text: Choose one object to carry today, like a pen, a stress ball, or sunflower seeds, so your hands have something to do instead of reaching for a pack.

tasks.title: Play a craving distraction game
tasks.text: When you feel restless today, open a mini game in the craving toolkit for two minutes instead of stepping outside for a smoke.

tasks.title: Rate today's cravings
tasks.text: Mark how strong your cravings felt today on a scale from one to five so you can see the trend later.

days.title: Day 6: Sleep and smoking
days.intro: Withdrawal can mess with your sleep for a little while. Knowing this in advance makes it less alarming when it happens.

tasks.title: Understand why sleep feels off
tasks.text: Nicotine affects sleep cycles, so some restlessness this week is normal withdrawal, not a sign something is wrong with you.

tasks.title: Try a wind down sound before bed
tasks.text: Play one relaxing sound from the toolkit tonight for five minutes before you try to sleep.

tasks.title: Note your energy levels
tasks.text: Write one line about how your energy felt today compared to day one.

days.title: Day 7: One week free
days.intro: Seven days without a cigarette. That is a real, measurable win, and your body has already started repairing itself in ways you cannot fully feel yet.

tasks.title: Claim your seven day badge
tasks.text: Open your badges tab and collect the one week milestone. You earned this one the hard way.

tasks.title: See what week one did for your body
tasks.text: Your sense of taste and smell are likely starting to improve and your lungs are beginning to clear out mucus and debris built up from smoking.

tasks.title: Write a note to day one you
tasks.text: Write two sentences to yourself from day one, telling them how week one actually went.

days.title: Day 8: Watch your guard
days.intro: A lot of people relapse right after the first big milestone because they feel like they have already won. Stay alert this week, not anxious, just alert.

tasks.title: Know the most common relapse trap
tasks.text: Many people who relapse do it in week two, often after one drink or one stressful moment, thinking just one cigarette will not matter. It usually restarts the whole habit.

tasks.title: Plan your next risky moment
tasks.text: Think of one event coming up this week where you might be tempted, like a party or a stressful meeting, and decide right now what you will do instead of smoking.

tasks.title: Log today's mood
tasks.text: Mark how you are feeling today in one tap so your coach can adjust your missions.

tasks.title: Practice a calm down even without a craving
tasks.text: Use the breathing tool once today even if you do not feel a craving, so it becomes second nature.

days.title: Day 9: Replace the ritual
days.intro: Smoking was never just nicotine, it was a ritual, a break, a pause button in your day. You need a new pause button.

tasks.title: Design your new break ritual
tasks.text: Pick one short activity to replace your old smoke break, like a two minute walk, stretching, or stepping outside for fresh air without a cigarette.

tasks.title: Write what you miss most
tasks.text: Be honest, write one sentence about what part of smoking you actually miss the most right now.

tasks.title: See your cigarettes not smoked
tasks.text: Check your stats to see roughly how many cigarettes you have avoided smoking so far.

tasks.title: Read one community story
tasks.text: Open the community tab and read one story from someone further along than you.

days.title: Day 10: Double digits
days.intro: Ten days. The physical nicotine withdrawal is mostly behind you now, the habit part is what you are working on.

tasks.title: Know what is left to deal with
tasks.text: Most of the physical nicotine withdrawal fades within the first one to two weeks, so what remains now is mostly habit and association, which is exactly what your missions are built to break.

tasks.title: Beat your craving game score
tasks.text: Open a mini game and try to beat your previous score during a free moment today.

tasks.title: Compare this week to last
tasks.text: Rate how this week felt overall compared to your first day.

tasks.title: Treat yourself with saved money
tasks.text: Look at your money saved and spend a small piece of it on something that has nothing to do with smoking.

days.title: Day 11: Boredom is a trigger too
days.intro: Stress gets blamed a lot, but plain boredom causes just as many cravings. Today is about catching that one.

tasks.title: Spot your boredom moments
tasks.text: Write down one moment today when you wanted a cigarette purely out of boredom, not stress.

tasks.title: Build a boredom list
tasks.text: Make a short list of three things you can do for two minutes when boredom hits, and save it somewhere you will see it.

tasks.title: Use sound to reset your focus
tasks.text: Play a focus or calm sound for five minutes during a slow part of your day.

tasks.title: See your streak
tasks.text: Look at your current streak number and notice it is the longest stretch without smoking you may have had in a long time.

days.title: Day 12: Cravings get shorter
days.intro: A craving usually peaks and fades within a few minutes if you do not act on it. The more you let them pass, the shorter they get.

tasks.title: Understand the craving wave
tasks.text: A craving typically rises and falls within roughly three to five minutes, which is why riding it out almost always works better than fighting it for hours in your head.

tasks.title: Time your next craving
tasks.text: Next time a craving hits, use the timer in the craving tool and watch how it actually fades.

tasks.title: Rate your confidence
tasks.text: Rate from one to five how confident you feel about staying smoke free this week.

tasks.title: Send encouragement to someone else
tasks.text: Find someone in the community on an earlier day than you and send them one encouraging message.

days.title: Day 13: Almost two weeks
days.intro: Tomorrow closes out the hardest chapter. Today is about noticing how far you already are from day one.

tasks.title: Compare day one to today
tasks.text: Write two or three sentences comparing how you felt on day one to how you feel right now.

tasks.title: Prepare for tomorrow's milestone
tasks.text: Plan one small way you want to mark hitting two weeks tomorrow, it can be as simple as telling someone or buying yourself something small.

tasks.title: See your health stats moving
tasks.text: Open your health progress and notice how many markers have already started improving.

tasks.title: Play one more round
tasks.text: Use a mini game once today purely as a small win, no craving required.

days.title: Day 14: Two weeks. Survival complete
days.intro: You just finished the hardest stretch of quitting. Nicotine withdrawal has done most of its damage already, and you outlasted it. Chapter two is about building the new normal.

tasks.title: Claim your two week badge
tasks.text: Open your badges tab and collect the two week milestone, this one marks the end of survival mode.

tasks.title: See how far your body has come
tasks.text: In two weeks your circulation and lung function have likely already started improving and your risk of a nicotine craving driven slip is lower than it was on day three.

tasks.title: Write your survival summary
tasks.text: Write three short sentences, what was hardest, what surprised you, and what you are proud of from these two weeks.

tasks.title: Look ahead to chapter two
tasks.text: Read the intro to your next chapter and set one intention for how you want the next two weeks to go.

chapters.name: Break the habit
chapters.role: New routines, morning/evening, replace smoke breaks

days.title: Day 15: Welcome to chapter two
days.intro: Survival mode is over. Now the real work begins, replacing the habits that smoking used to fill, one routine at a time.

tasks.title: Map your old smoking schedule
tasks.text: Write down the times of day you used to smoke most, like waking up, after meals, or during work breaks.

tasks.title: Pick your hardest hour
tasks.text: Choose the one hour of the day that is still hardest for you and decide on one specific replacement action for it.

tasks.title: See your chapter one stats
tasks.text: Open your stats and look at total smoke free days, money saved, and cigarettes avoided from chapter one.

tasks.title: Set your chapter two goal
tasks.text: Write or pick one personal goal you want to hit by day thirty.

days.title: Day 16: The morning routine
days.intro: Mornings are often the strongest smoking ritual, tied to waking up, coffee, or the first stress of the day.

tasks.title: Redesign your first ten minutes
tasks.text: Plan exactly what you will do in the first ten minutes after waking up tomorrow instead of reaching for a cigarette.

tasks.title: Know why mornings are hard
tasks.text: Many smokers associate the first cigarette of the day with waking up the brain, so replacing it with movement or water can help your body get the same wake up signal.

tasks.title: Try a morning breathing reset
tasks.text: Use the breathing tool for one minute tomorrow morning before checking your phone.

tasks.title: Rate this morning
tasks.text: Rate how this morning felt without a cigarette compared to a normal morning before.

days.title: Day 17: After meals
days.intro: After meals is one of the most automatic smoking triggers there is. Today you build a new ending to your meals.

tasks.title: Pick a new after meal habit
tasks.text: Choose one thing to do right after eating instead of smoking, like brushing your teeth, chewing gum, or a short walk.

tasks.title: Notice the pull after eating
tasks.text: Write one line about how strong the urge was after your biggest meal today.

tasks.title: See your taste and smell progress
tasks.text: Many ex smokers notice food tasting better within the first few weeks as smell and taste receptors recover.

tasks.title: Use a game after lunch
tasks.text: If a craving hits after your meal today, open a mini game for two minutes instead.

days.title: Day 18: The commute trigger
days.intro: Driving, walking to work, or waiting for the bus used to come with a cigarette for a lot of smokers. Today is about that gap.

tasks.title: Plan your commute differently
tasks.text: Decide on one small change for your commute today, like a podcast, music, or a different route.

tasks.title: Log a trigger you noticed
tasks.text: Tap to log any trigger moment you noticed today, even small ones.

tasks.title: See your streak growing
tasks.text: Open your streak counter and notice it is now longer than your average gap between cigarettes used to be.

tasks.title: Try a sound during your commute
tasks.text: Play a calming sound during part of your commute today.

days.title: Day 19: Stress without smoking
days.intro: A lot of people used cigarettes as their main stress tool. Today is about finding what else can do that job.

tasks.title: Use breathing for stress, not just cravings
tasks.text: Next time you feel stressed today, even without a craving, try the breathing tool.

tasks.title: Name your stress source
tasks.text: Write down the main thing causing you stress this week.

tasks.title: Know the stress myth
tasks.text: Cigarettes do not actually reduce stress, the brief relief comes from relieving withdrawal symptoms the previous cigarette caused, which means your stress levels can improve once you are fully nicotine free.

tasks.title: Try one non smoking stress tool
tasks.text: Pick one stress reliever to try today that has nothing to do with the craving toolkit, like a short walk or calling a friend.

days.title: Day 20: Twenty days in
days.intro: Three weeks of new habits forming. This is roughly when new routines start to feel less forced.

tasks.title: Rate how automatic your new habits feel
tasks.text: Rate from one to five how natural your replacement habits feel compared to two weeks ago.

tasks.title: See your money milestone
tasks.text: Check your money saved tab and see what that amount could buy you right now.

tasks.title: Write your easiest win
tasks.text: Write about the one replacement habit that has worked best for you so far.

tasks.title: Share a small win
tasks.text: Post one small win from this week in the community.

days.title: Day 21: Three weeks free
days.intro: Three weeks is often talked about as the point where a new habit starts to take hold. You are proof it can.

tasks.title: Claim your three week badge
tasks.text: Open your badges tab and collect the three week milestone.

tasks.title: See your lung progress
tasks.text: Around this stage many people notice less coughing and easier breathing during light activity as lung function continues to recover.

tasks.title: Test yourself in a real situation
tasks.text: Put yourself in a mildly triggering situation today on purpose, like sitting near where people smoke, and notice that you can handle it.

tasks.title: Rate your overall mood this week
tasks.text: Rate how your mood has been this week on a simple scale.

days.title: Day 22: Evening wind down
days.intro: Evenings often had their own smoking ritual, the end of work, the after dinner cigarette, the wind down before bed.

tasks.title: Build an evening ritual
tasks.text: Choose one calming activity to do every evening instead of an end of day cigarette, like tea, a show, or a short walk.

tasks.title: Try a sleep sound tonight
tasks.text: Play a relaxing sound from the toolkit for ten minutes before bed.

tasks.title: Note your sleep quality
tasks.text: Write one line about how you have been sleeping this past week.

tasks.title: See your full week trend
tasks.text: Open your weekly stats and look at how your craving intensity has trended over the past seven days.

days.title: Day 23: Social smoking habits
days.intro: Some cravings are not really about nicotine at all, they are about being around other people who smoke.

tasks.title: Think about your smoking friends
tasks.text: Write down who in your life still smokes and how often you are around them.

tasks.title: Plan your next hangout
tasks.text: If you know you will be around a smoker soon, decide now what you will do during their smoke break instead of joining them.

tasks.title: Know it gets easier with practice
tasks.text: Each time you get through a social smoking moment without lighting up, the automatic urge tied to that specific situation gets a little weaker.

tasks.title: Rate your social confidence
tasks.text: Rate how confident you feel being around smokers without smoking yourself.

days.title: Day 24: Boredom and downtime
days.intro: Now that the big triggers are getting easier, the quieter ones like boredom start showing up more clearly.

tasks.title: Update your boredom list
tasks.text: Add one new activity to your boredom list from chapter one based on what you have learned so far.

tasks.title: Use a game during downtime
tasks.text: Next time you have a quiet moment with nothing to do, open a mini game instead of feeling restless.

tasks.title: Log today's craving count
tasks.text: Log roughly how many cravings you noticed today, even mild ones.

tasks.title: See your progress chart
tasks.text: Look at your craving frequency chart and notice the overall direction since day one.

days.title: Day 25: What you have replaced
days.intro: By now you likely have several small new habits running in the background. Today is about noticing them.

tasks.title: List your new habits
tasks.text: Write down every small replacement habit you have built so far, even tiny ones.

tasks.title: See your cigarettes avoided
tasks.text: Open your stats and see roughly how many cigarettes you have not smoked since starting.

tasks.title: Strengthen your weakest habit
tasks.text: Pick the replacement habit that feels least solid and do it on purpose today, even without a craving.

tasks.title: Read about someone in chapter two
tasks.text: Read one community post from someone also in their first month.

days.title: Day 26: Alcohol and smoking links
days.intro: For a lot of people, drinking and smoking were tightly linked. This trigger deserves its own attention before it catches you off guard.

tasks.title: Know the alcohol risk
tasks.text: Drinking lowers inhibition and is one of the most common situations linked to relapse, because the automatic hand to mouth habit can return without you fully deciding it.

tasks.title: Make a drinking plan
tasks.text: If you plan to drink soon, decide in advance how you will handle the moment when others light up around you.

tasks.title: Rate this trigger's strength for you
tasks.text: Rate from one to five how strong the alcohol and smoking link feels for you personally.

tasks.title: Recall a past drinking and smoking moment
tasks.text: Write about one specific memory of smoking while drinking, and what you could do differently next time.

days.title: Day 27: Almost one month
days.intro: You are days away from your first full month. Most of the worst of the physical habit is behind you now.

tasks.title: Look back at chapter two
tasks.text: Write two or three sentences about what changed for you during this habit building chapter.

tasks.title: See your health timeline
tasks.text: Open your health progress tab and see which markers have moved the most in the last two weeks.

tasks.title: Prepare for the one month mark
tasks.text: Decide how you want to mark hitting one full month, even something small.

tasks.title: Rate your readiness for chapter three
tasks.text: Rate how ready you feel to handle social situations and stress without smoking.

days.title: Day 28: Four weeks free
days.intro: Four full weeks. Your daily life now runs on habits that do not include cigarettes, even if some days are still harder than others.

tasks.title: Claim your four week badge
tasks.text: Open your badges tab and collect this milestone.

tasks.title: See your overall risk drop
tasks.text: Within the first month, the risk of certain heart related issues linked to smoking already begins to decrease compared to someone who continues smoking.

tasks.title: Share your one month story
tasks.text: Post a short update in the community about reaching four weeks.

tasks.title: Celebrate with a quick game
tasks.text: Play a mini game just for fun today, no craving needed.

days.title: Day 29: Tools you trust now
days.intro: You have used a lot of tools over the past month. Today is about knowing which ones actually work for you.

tasks.title: Rank your go to tools
tasks.text: Write down which craving tools, breathing, games, or sounds have worked best for you personally.

tasks.title: Set a chapter three intention
tasks.text: Write or pick one thing you want to focus on as you move into social situations and stress.

tasks.title: See your full month numbers
tasks.text: Open your stats and look at total days, money saved, and cigarettes avoided over the past month.

tasks.title: Plan one upcoming challenge
tasks.text: Think of one event coming up in the next month that could be a real test, and note it down.

days.title: Day 30: One month smoke free
days.intro: Thirty days. A full month without a single cigarette. You did not just survive, you built new habits that are starting to feel normal. Chapter three is about proving they hold up under real pressure.

tasks.title: Claim your one month badge
tasks.text: Open your badges tab and collect the one month milestone, one of the biggest ones yet.

tasks.title: See your one month transformation
tasks.text: Open your full health and stats overview and see everything that has changed for you in just thirty days.

tasks.title: Write a letter to day one you
tasks.text: Write a short letter to yourself on day one, telling them what the first month was really like.

tasks.title: Look ahead to chapter three
tasks.text: Read the chapter three intro and set one goal for handling social situations smoke free.

chapters.name: New normal
chapters.role: Social situations, stress, alcohol, work, stay smoke-free

days.title: Day 31: Welcome to chapter three
days.intro: The habit building phase is done. Now it is about proving your new normal holds up in real situations, not just quiet routines.

tasks.title: List your upcoming social events
tasks.text: Write down any parties, dinners, or gatherings coming up in the next two weeks.

tasks.title: Know what chapter three covers
tasks.text: This chapter focuses on the situations that trip up a lot of quitters after the first month, like parties, drinking, stress at work, and being around old smoking friends.

tasks.title: Set your chapter three goal
tasks.text: Pick one specific situation you want to handle smoke free this month.

tasks.title: Prepare one social script
tasks.text: Write one short sentence you can say if someone offers you a cigarette, so you do not have to think of it on the spot.

days.title: Day 32: Saying no without explaining
days.intro: You do not owe anyone a long explanation for not smoking. A short, confident no is enough.

tasks.title: Practice your no
tasks.text: Say your prepared response out loud once today so it feels natural if you need it.

tasks.title: Know you do not need to justify it
tasks.text: Quitting is a complete reason on its own, you are allowed to decline without giving a backstory.

tasks.title: Rate your confidence in social settings
tasks.text: Rate from one to five how confident you feel turning down a cigarette in front of others.

days.title: Day 33: Old smoking friends
days.intro: Some friendships were built partly around smoking together. That does not mean the friendship has to end, but it might need to change shape.

tasks.title: Think about one specific friend
tasks.text: Write about one friend you used to smoke with and how your time together might look now.

tasks.title: Suggest a different hangout
tasks.text: If you are seeing a smoking friend soon, suggest doing something that is not centered around smoke breaks.

tasks.title: Know this gets easier
tasks.text: The strong pull to join a friend's smoke break usually fades the more times you are around it without smoking yourself.

days.title: Day 34: Stress at work
days.intro: Work stress used to send a lot of people straight to a cigarette break. Today is about a different release valve.

tasks.title: Use breathing during a work stress moment
tasks.text: Next time work stress hits today, step away for one minute and use the breathing tool instead of a smoke break.

tasks.title: Take a real break, just not a smoke one
tasks.text: Take a two minute walk away from your desk today as your new version of a break.

tasks.title: Log your stress level today
tasks.text: Rate how stressful work felt today on a simple scale.

days.title: Day 35: Five weeks free
days.intro: Five weeks in, and you have already handled more triggering situations than you probably expected to.

tasks.title: Claim your five week badge
tasks.text: Open your badges tab and collect this milestone.

tasks.title: See your progress so far
tasks.text: Open your stats and look at your full streak alongside your money saved and cigarettes avoided.

tasks.title: Encourage someone newer than you
tasks.text: Find someone in their first two weeks and send them one encouraging message.

days.title: Day 36: Drinking out
days.intro: Going out for drinks is one of the highest risk situations for relapse. Today is about going in with a plan.

tasks.title: Set a drink limit if you are going out
tasks.text: If you are drinking soon, decide your limit in advance, since lower inhibition makes old habits easier to slip back into.

tasks.title: Know the real risk window
tasks.text: The risk moment is usually not the first drink, it is later in the night when tiredness and lowered guard combine with people smoking outside.

tasks.title: Rate how risky tonight feels
tasks.text: If you are going out tonight, rate how risky the situation feels for you in advance.

days.title: Day 37: After a night out
days.intro: If last night was a test, today is about checking in honestly, whether it went well or not.

tasks.title: Reflect on last night
tasks.text: Write about how last night went if you were in a social or drinking situation, including any close calls.

tasks.title: A close call is not a failure
tasks.text: Feeling tempted and not smoking is a win on its own, even if it felt hard, it still counts as a successful day.

days.title: Day 38: Celebrations and good news
days.intro: People often forget that good moments, not just stressful ones, used to come with a cigarette too.

tasks.title: Notice the celebration trigger
tasks.text: Write down if you have ever wanted to smoke after good news rather than bad, and what that felt like.

tasks.title: Plan a new way to celebrate
tasks.text: Pick one new way to mark good news that has nothing to do with smoking, like a favorite snack or telling someone.

tasks.title: Know both ends of the trigger
tasks.text: Smoking habits often get triggered by strong emotion in either direction, both stress and excitement, so both deserve a plan.

days.title: Day 39: Family gatherings
days.intro: Family events can bring out old habits fast, especially around relatives who still smoke.

tasks.title: Prepare for your next family event
tasks.text: If a family gathering is coming up, decide where you will go and what you will do during any smoke breaks others take.

tasks.title: Rate family pressure
tasks.text: Rate how much pressure you feel from family or relatives around your quitting.

days.title: Day 40: Forty days strong
days.intro: Forty days is a serious stretch by any measure. Patterns that used to run your day automatically no longer do.

tasks.title: See how your lungs are doing
tasks.text: By this stage many ex smokers notice noticeably easier breathing during light exercise as airways continue to heal.

tasks.title: Write your biggest surprise
tasks.text: Write about the thing that has surprised you most since you quit, good or hard.

tasks.title: Test a harder situation on purpose
tasks.text: Put yourself in a moderately triggering situation on purpose today and notice you get through it.

days.title: Day 41: The one cigarette myth
days.intro: Just one will not hurt is one of the most dangerous thoughts a quitter can have. Today is about understanding why.

tasks.title: Know why one is rarely just one
tasks.text: Nicotine reactivates the brain's craving pathways quickly, which is why one cigarette after weeks off often leads straight back to daily smoking rather than staying a one time thing.

tasks.title: Write your own warning note
tasks.text: Write a short note to your future self about why one cigarette is not worth the risk, to read if you are ever tempted.

days.title: Day 42: Six weeks free
days.intro: Six weeks. Your body chemistry, your routines, and your confidence have all shifted since day one.

tasks.title: Claim your six week badge
tasks.text: Open your badges tab and collect this milestone.

tasks.title: See your numbers at six weeks
tasks.text: Open your stats tab and look at your full progress, money, days, and cigarettes avoided.

tasks.title: Share a six week update
tasks.text: Post a short update in the community about reaching six weeks.

days.title: Day 43: Travel and routine breaks
days.intro: Travel, even for fun, breaks your normal routine, and broken routines can loosen the grip of new habits.

tasks.title: Plan for your next trip
tasks.text: If you have travel coming up, think about which of your usual routines will be missing and what you will do instead.

tasks.title: Rate how stable your routine feels
tasks.text: Rate how solid your smoke free routine feels right now, even without travel.

days.title: Day 44: Identity check in
days.intro: Somewhere around now, many people start thinking of themselves less as a smoker who quit and more as simply a non smoker.

tasks.title: How do you describe yourself now
tasks.text: Write down how you would describe your relationship with smoking today compared to two months ago.

tasks.title: Identity matters more than willpower
tasks.text: Long term quitters often describe a shift from fighting cravings to simply being someone who does not smoke, which takes less daily effort than constant willpower.

days.title: Day 45: Halfway to chapter four
days.intro: You are halfway through chapter three. Stress, social pressure, and alcohol have all come up by now, and you have handled them.

tasks.title: Rate this chapter so far
tasks.text: Rate how chapter three has gone for you overall compared to chapter two.

tasks.title: See your stats halfway through chapter three
tasks.text: Check your full stats overview and notice your trend since day thirty one.

tasks.title: Take a quick mental break
tasks.text: Play a mini game for two minutes just to reset, no craving required.

days.title: Day 46: Anger and irritability
days.intro: Some people used cigarettes to cool down after getting angry or frustrated. That release needs a new outlet too.

tasks.title: Use breathing for anger, not just craving
tasks.text: Next time you feel frustrated today, use the breathing tool before reacting.

tasks.title: Recall an angry smoking moment
tasks.text: Write about a time you used to smoke specifically because you were angry or frustrated.

days.title: Day 47: Weekend triggers
days.intro: Weekends often had a different smoking rhythm than weekdays, more free time, more social time, more downtime.

tasks.title: Plan your weekend differently
tasks.text: Think about your usual weekend pattern and pick one part of it to handle differently this week.

tasks.title: Rate weekend difficulty
tasks.text: Rate how hard weekends feel for you compared to weekdays right now.

days.title: Day 48: Seven weeks free
days.intro: Seven weeks. The space between you and your last cigarette keeps growing, and so does your evidence that you can do this.

tasks.title: Claim your seven week badge
tasks.text: Open your badges tab and collect this milestone.

tasks.title: See your circulation improving
tasks.text: By this stage circulation has generally improved further, which can make physical activity feel noticeably easier than it did when you smoked.

days.title: Day 49: Coffee and smoking
days.intro: Coffee and cigarettes were a classic pair for a lot of smokers. If that link is still strong for you, today is about loosening it.

tasks.title: Check your coffee link
tasks.text: Write down whether you still feel a pull to smoke specifically when drinking coffee.

tasks.title: Change your coffee setting
tasks.text: Try drinking your coffee in a different location or with a different activity today.

days.title: Day 50: Fifty days
days.intro: Fifty days without a cigarette is a number a lot of people never reach. You are well past it.

tasks.title: See your full fifty day overview
tasks.text: Open your stats and look at everything you have built since day one, streak, money, and health markers.

tasks.title: Write your fifty day reflection
tasks.text: Write a few sentences on what has changed in how you think about smoking since you started.

tasks.title: Share your fifty day milestone
tasks.text: Post an update in the community about reaching fifty days.

days.title: Day 51: Boredom revisited
days.intro: Boredom triggers tend to come back in new forms as life settles into a routine again.

tasks.title: Rate today's boredom level
tasks.text: Rate how bored you felt today and whether it connected to any craving.

tasks.title: Use a game for boredom
tasks.text: Next time boredom hits today, use a mini game instead of letting your mind wander toward smoking.

days.title: Day 52: Watching others smoke
days.intro: Seeing someone else smoke can still trigger a flicker of craving even after weeks free. That flicker does not mean you are failing.

tasks.title: Know that visual triggers are normal
tasks.text: Seeing or smelling someone else's cigarette can trigger a brief urge even long after quitting, this is a normal association, not a sign you are about to relapse.

tasks.title: Describe your reaction
tasks.text: Write about how you felt the last time you saw someone smoking nearby.

days.title: Day 53: Your support system
days.intro: Quitting is easier with people around you who know what you are doing and why.

tasks.title: Connect with the community
tasks.text: Comment on or react to two other people's posts in the community today.

tasks.title: Who supports you most
tasks.text: Write down who in your life has been most supportive of your quitting so far.

days.title: Day 54: Eight weeks free
days.intro: Eight weeks. Two full months of mornings, meals, stress, and nights out, all without a cigarette.

tasks.title: Claim your eight week badge
tasks.text: Open your badges tab and collect this milestone.

tasks.title: See your two month health gains
tasks.text: Open your health progress tab and see how far your key markers have moved over two months.

days.title: Day 55: Slips happen, plans matter
days.intro: Even with a strong streak, it helps to know exactly what you would do if you ever did slip.

tasks.title: Write your slip recovery plan
tasks.text: Write down exactly what you would do in the first hour after a slip, who you would tell and what your next step would be.

tasks.title: A slip is not the end
tasks.text: Many successful quitters had at least one slip along the way, what mattered most was getting back to zero immediately instead of treating it as total failure.

days.title: Day 56: Reviewing chapter three
days.intro: You are almost through chapter three. Social pressure, stress, alcohol, and old habits have all been tested.

tasks.title: Pick your hardest situation this chapter
tasks.text: Write about the single hardest situation you faced in chapter three and how you got through it.

tasks.title: Rate your overall chapter three
tasks.text: Rate chapter three overall on how well you think you handled it.

days.title: Day 57: Confidence check
days.intro: By now you have real evidence, not just hope, that you can handle hard moments without smoking.

tasks.title: Look at your evidence
tasks.text: Open your stats and count how many days you have now successfully gotten through, each one is proof.

tasks.title: Rate your confidence for the future
tasks.text: Rate how confident you feel about staying smoke free for the next thirty days.

days.title: Day 58: Almost two months
days.intro: Two days from a two month milestone. Worth noticing how much less you think about cigarettes day to day now.

tasks.title: How often do you think about it now
tasks.text: Write about how often cigarettes cross your mind now compared to your first week.

tasks.title: Plan your two month mark
tasks.text: Decide how you want to acknowledge hitting two full months in two days.

days.title: Day 59: One day to go
days.intro: Tomorrow closes chapter three. You have made it through the situations most likely to cause a relapse.

tasks.title: Know what is coming next
tasks.text: Chapter four focuses on relapse traps, boredom, and celebrations, building toward your three month milestone.

tasks.title: Rate how ready you feel
tasks.text: Rate how ready you feel for the next chapter.

days.title: Day 60: Two months smoke free
days.intro: Sixty days. You have handled parties, drinks, stress, family, and boredom, all without smoking. That is not luck, that is a skill you have built.

tasks.title: Claim your two month badge
tasks.text: Open your badges tab and collect this major milestone.

tasks.title: See your two month transformation
tasks.text: Open your full stats and health overview to see everything that has changed since day one.

tasks.title: Write your chapter three summary
tasks.text: Write a few sentences summarizing what you learned during chapter three.

tasks.title: Look ahead to chapter four
tasks.text: Read the chapter four intro and set one goal for staying strong toward your three month mark.

days.title: Day 61: Welcome to chapter four
days.intro: You are in the stretch where confidence is high and that is exactly when guard can slip. This chapter is about staying sharp on the way to three months.

tasks.title: Know the complacency trap
tasks.text: Many relapses happen after the two month mark, not because life gets harder, but because people stop treating cravings seriously once they feel like they have already won.

tasks.title: Set your chapter four goal
tasks.text: Pick one thing you want to stay alert about over the next month.

tasks.title: Name your current biggest risk
tasks.text: Write down the one situation you think is most likely to challenge you in the next thirty days.

days.title: Day 62: The just checking trap
days.intro: Some people convince themselves that having just one to test their willpower is harmless curiosity. It rarely is.

tasks.title: Know why testing yourself backfires
tasks.text: Trying a single cigarette to prove you can handle it puts nicotine back in your system, which can trigger real cravings again rather than proving anything.

tasks.title: Have you had this thought
tasks.text: Write honestly whether the idea of just one to test yourself has crossed your mind recently.

days.title: Day 63: Boredom as a long game
days.intro: Boredom does not go away forever, it just becomes less frequent. Today is about keeping your boredom tools sharp.

tasks.title: Refresh your boredom toolkit
tasks.text: Try a mini game you have not used in a while during a slow moment today.

tasks.title: Add a new boredom activity
tasks.text: Add one new activity to your boredom list that you have not tried before.

days.title: Day 64: Nine weeks free
days.intro: Nine weeks. Your old smoking schedule probably feels distant by now.

tasks.title: Claim your nine week badge
tasks.text: Open your badges tab and collect this milestone.

tasks.title: See your progress at nine weeks
tasks.text: Open your stats and review your streak, money saved, and health markers.

days.title: Day 65: Celebration triggers again
days.intro: Good news, promotions, achievements, and parties can quietly bring back the urge to celebrate the old way.

tasks.title: Recall a recent good moment
tasks.text: Write about a recent piece of good news and whether any urge to smoke came with it.

tasks.title: Plan your next celebration
tasks.text: Decide in advance how you will celebrate your three month milestone when it arrives.

days.title: Day 66: Holidays and special days
days.intro: Special occasions, even small ones, can carry old associations with smoking.

tasks.title: Rate upcoming occasion risk
tasks.text: If you have a birthday, holiday, or event coming up soon, rate how risky it feels.

tasks.title: Plan beats willpower
tasks.text: Going into a special occasion with a plan for smoke breaks and toasts works better than relying purely on willpower in the moment.

days.title: Day 67: Old friends, old habits
days.intro: Reconnecting with someone from your smoking past can bring back more than just memories.

tasks.title: Think about an old smoking friend
tasks.text: Write about anyone from your past you associate strongly with smoking, even if you do not see them often now.

tasks.title: Decide your approach in advance
tasks.text: If you might see that person soon, decide now how you will handle it if they offer you a cigarette.

days.title: Day 68: Ten weeks free
days.intro: Ten weeks. You are deep into proving this is not a phase, it is who you are now.

tasks.title: Claim your ten week badge
tasks.text: Open your badges tab and collect this milestone.

tasks.title: See your full ten week stats
tasks.text: Open your stats tab and review everything you have built over ten weeks.

days.title: Day 69: Tiredness and low energy
days.intro: Being exhausted lowers everyone's guard, including around old habits.

tasks.title: Notice tiredness and cravings
tasks.text: Write down whether you have noticed any link between being very tired and wanting a cigarette.

tasks.title: Rest with a calming sound
tasks.text: Use a relaxing sound for a few minutes today if you are feeling run down.

days.title: Day 70: Seventy days strong
days.intro: Seventy days. The number itself is a reminder of how consistent you have been.

tasks.title: See your seventy day overview
tasks.text: Open your stats and look at your full progress across streak, money, and health.

tasks.title: Share a seventy day update
tasks.text: Post a quick update in the community about hitting seventy days.

days.title: Day 71: Watching for warning signs
days.intro: Small warning signs, like more frequent thoughts about smoking, are worth catching early.

tasks.title: Rate your current craving frequency
tasks.text: Rate how often you have thought about smoking in the past three days.

tasks.title: Address any rising risk
tasks.text: If your cravings have felt stronger lately, pick one extra tool to use this week, like more breathing sessions or community check ins.

days.title: Day 72: The mental bargaining trap
days.intro: After a while just this once thoughts can get more convincing sounding, even though the risk has not changed.

tasks.title: Know the bargaining pattern
tasks.text: The mind sometimes builds a very convincing case for one exception, special occasion, bad day, just this once, but the underlying risk to your streak stays the same no matter how reasonable it sounds.

tasks.title: Write your counter argument
tasks.text: Write one strong sentence to counter any just this once thought, to have ready in advance.

days.title: Day 73: Checking your why
days.intro: Reconnecting with your original reason for quitting keeps it from fading into the background.

tasks.title: Revisit your original reason
tasks.text: Write down the main reason you decided to quit in the first place, and whether it still feels just as important now.

tasks.title: See your saved money grow
tasks.text: Open your money saved tab and notice how much it has grown since day one.

days.title: Day 74: Eleven weeks free
days.intro: Eleven weeks. One more week stands between you and three full months.

tasks.title: Claim your eleven week badge
tasks.text: Open your badges tab and collect this milestone.

tasks.title: Rate your readiness for three months
tasks.text: Rate how ready you feel for the three month milestone coming up.

days.title: Day 75: Helping someone else
days.intro: Supporting another person trying to quit can strengthen your own resolve at the same time.

tasks.title: Support someone earlier in their journey
tasks.text: Find someone in their first month and offer one piece of encouragement or advice.

tasks.title: What would you tell day one you
tasks.text: Write the single most useful thing you would tell yourself on day one, knowing what you know now.

days.title: Day 76: Physical activity boost
days.intro: Many people notice their physical stamina improving noticeably by this stage.

tasks.title: See your stamina gains
tasks.text: By around three months, lung function for many ex smokers has improved enough that everyday activities like stairs or brisk walking feel noticeably easier.

tasks.title: Test your stamina
tasks.text: Do one physical activity today, even a short walk or stairs, and notice how it feels compared to when you smoked.

days.title: Day 77: Mental clarity check
days.intro: Improved focus and mental clarity are commonly reported benefits around this stage of quitting.

tasks.title: Notice your focus
tasks.text: Write about whether your concentration or mental clarity has felt different since you quit.

tasks.title: Rate your overall wellbeing
tasks.text: Rate how you feel overall today on a simple scale.

days.title: Day 78: Twelve weeks free
days.intro: Twelve weeks. Three months are now just two days away.

tasks.title: Claim your twelve week badge
tasks.text: Open your badges tab and collect this milestone.

tasks.title: Finalize your three month plan
tasks.text: Decide exactly how you want to mark hitting three full months in two days.

days.title: Day 79: One day before three months
days.intro: Tomorrow is a major milestone. Today is just about staying steady.

tasks.title: Look back at your whole journey
tasks.text: Open your stats and scroll through your entire history from day one to today.

tasks.title: Write what tomorrow means to you
tasks.text: Write a sentence or two about what reaching three months represents for you personally.

days.title: Day 80: Three months smoke free
days.intro: Ninety days. A full quarter of a year without a single cigarette. This is one of the biggest milestones in quitting, both medically and mentally.

tasks.title: Claim your three month badge
tasks.text: Open your badges tab and collect this major milestone.

tasks.title: See your three month transformation
tasks.text: By three months, lung function and circulation have generally improved substantially for most ex smokers compared to when they were still smoking.

tasks.title: Share your three month milestone
tasks.text: Post your three month update in the community.

tasks.title: Write your full journey summary
tasks.text: Write a few sentences summarizing your journey from day one to day ninety.

days.title: Day 81: After the big milestone
days.intro: It is normal for motivation to dip slightly right after a major milestone passes. Knowing this in advance helps.

tasks.title: Know the post milestone dip
tasks.text: Motivation often drops slightly after a big milestone passes simply because the immediate goal is gone, this is normal and temporary.

tasks.title: Set your next personal goal
tasks.text: Pick a new personal goal to aim for now that three months is behind you.

days.title: Day 82: Routine maintenance
days.intro: At this stage, the goal shifts from building new habits to simply maintaining the ones that work.

tasks.title: List your core habits
tasks.text: Write down the three or four replacement habits that have become most automatic for you.

tasks.title: Keep one habit fresh
tasks.text: Do one of your core replacement habits on purpose today, even without needing it.

days.title: Day 83: Long term money goal
days.intro: Three months of saved money adds up to a real amount. Today is about thinking bigger with it.

tasks.title: See your three month savings
tasks.text: Open your money saved tab and look at the total since day one.

tasks.title: Set a savings goal
tasks.text: Pick something specific you want to put your smoking money toward over the next few months.

days.title: Day 84: Twelve full weeks plus
days.intro: You are well past three months now, deep into territory where smoking is genuinely becoming part of your past.

tasks.title: Rate how distant smoking feels
tasks.text: Rate how far away your smoking days feel compared to right after you quit.

tasks.title: Quick mental reset
tasks.text: Play a mini game for a couple minutes just as a small break in your day.

days.title: Day 85: Watching for boredom relapse
days.intro: Even at this stage, plain boredom remains one of the sneakier relapse triggers.

tasks.title: Boredom never fully disappears
tasks.text: Even experienced ex smokers can feel an occasional pull during very boring stretches, having a plan ready matters more than expecting the urge to vanish completely.

tasks.title: Refresh your distraction list
tasks.text: Update your list of go to activities for boring moments with anything new you have discovered.

days.title: Day 86: Reflecting on identity
days.intro: Many people notice that by now, they think of themselves simply as someone who does not smoke, rather than someone fighting urges all day.

tasks.title: How would a stranger describe you
tasks.text: Write how you think someone meeting you today, with no history, would describe your relationship with smoking.

tasks.title: Identity shift is a real milestone
tasks.text: Shifting from quitting smoker to simply non smoker in your own mind is one of the strongest predictors of staying smoke free long term.

days.title: Day 87: Helping shape your plan
days.intro: You have been following missions for almost three months now. Today is about noticing what you actually need going forward.

tasks.title: Rate which tools you still use
tasks.text: Rate how often you still use the craving toolkit compared to your first month.

tasks.title: What do you need less of now
tasks.text: Write about which part of the app or plan you feel you need less support from now.

days.title: Day 88: Almost chapter five
days.intro: Chapter four is almost done. The next chapter moves into identity, health wins, and confidence as a non smoker.

tasks.title: Know what is coming next
tasks.text: Chapter five focuses on identity as a non smoker, ongoing health wins, and building lasting confidence.

tasks.title: Set an intention for chapter five
tasks.text: Write one intention for how you want to think about yourself going into the next chapter.

days.title: Day 89: One day before the end of chapter four
days.intro: Tomorrow wraps up a chapter built around staying sharp during the highest complacency risk window.

tasks.title: Reflect on staying strong
tasks.text: Write about a moment in this chapter where you almost let your guard down but did not.

tasks.title: Rate chapter four overall
tasks.text: Rate how well you think you handled chapter four.

days.title: Day 90: Three months and counting
days.intro: Ninety days behind you, and the riskiest complacency window has passed with your streak intact. From here, the work shifts from staying strong to truly becoming who you are now.

tasks.title: Claim your ninety day badge
tasks.text: Open your badges tab and collect this milestone.

tasks.title: See your full ninety day overview
tasks.text: Open your stats and look at everything across streak, money, cigarettes avoided, and health since day one.

tasks.title: Share your chapter four completion
tasks.text: Post in the community about finishing chapter four and reaching the three month mark.

tasks.title: Look ahead to chapter five
tasks.text: Read the chapter five intro and set one goal around your identity as a non smoker.

chapters.name: Who you are now
chapters.role: Identity as non-smoker, health wins, confidence

days.title: Day 91: Welcome to chapter five
days.intro: This chapter is less about fighting cravings and more about settling into who you are now, a non smoker, not a smoker who is resisting.

tasks.title: Finish this sentence
tasks.text: Write a few words completing this sentence, I am someone who.

tasks.title: Set your chapter five goal
tasks.text: Pick one thing you want to focus on around identity and confidence this month.

days.title: Day 92: Your health report card
days.intro: Three months in, your body has made real, measurable progress.

tasks.title: Review your key health gains
tasks.text: Open your health progress tab and review every marker that has improved since day one.

tasks.title: Which change matters most to you
tasks.text: Write about which physical change you have noticed has meant the most to you personally.

days.title: Day 93: No longer the exception
days.intro: Turning down a cigarette no longer needs to feel like a special act of willpower, it is simply what you do.

tasks.title: Rate how automatic saying no feels
tasks.text: Rate how automatic it feels to decline a cigarette now compared to your first month.

tasks.title: Notice it happen without effort
tasks.text: Pay attention today to any moment where you did not even consciously think about not smoking, it simply did not come up.

days.title: Day 94: Thirteen weeks free
days.intro: Thirteen weeks. A full quarter year and one extra week.

tasks.title: Claim your thirteen week badge
tasks.text: Open your badges tab and collect this milestone.

tasks.title: See your thirteen week numbers
tasks.text: Open your stats and review your streak, money, and cigarettes avoided.

days.title: Day 95: Confidence in new situations
days.intro: By now you have likely faced a new situation, a new job, a new social group, fully smoke free from the start.

tasks.title: Recall a new situation handled smoke free
tasks.text: Write about any new situation you have entered since quitting and handled without smoking.

tasks.title: This is proof, not luck
tasks.text: Successfully navigating new situations smoke free is direct evidence of a stable new identity, not a coincidence.

days.title: Day 96: Physical performance check
days.intro: Stamina and recovery from exercise often continue improving well past the three month mark.

tasks.title: Push your activity a little
tasks.text: Do a slightly more demanding physical activity than usual today and notice how your body responds.

tasks.title: Rate your physical stamina
tasks.text: Rate how your overall stamina feels compared to when you smoked.

days.title: Day 97: Skin and appearance
days.intro: Smoking affects more than lungs, skin and overall appearance often improve too over time.

tasks.title: Know the appearance benefits
tasks.text: Better blood flow and oxygen delivery after quitting can lead to improved skin tone and slower visible aging compared to continued smoking.

tasks.title: Have you noticed a change
tasks.text: Write about whether anyone has commented on your appearance since you quit, or if you have noticed anything yourself.

days.title: Day 98: Fourteen weeks free
days.intro: Fourteen weeks. Each one adds more proof that this is simply how you live now.

tasks.title: Claim your fourteen week badge
tasks.text: Open your badges tab and collect this milestone.

tasks.title: Share a confidence win
tasks.text: Post in the community about a moment recently where you felt fully confident as a non smoker.

days.title: Day 99: Mentoring others
days.intro: By now, you likely have real, specific advice that could help someone just starting out.

tasks.title: Give specific advice to a beginner
tasks.text: Find someone in chapter one or two and give them one specific tip that worked for you.

tasks.title: Write your top three tips
tasks.text: Write the three pieces of advice you would give anyone starting day one today.

days.title: Day 100: One hundred days
days.intro: One hundred days without a cigarette. This number alone tells a clear story about who you have become.

tasks.title: Claim your one hundred day badge
tasks.text: Open your badges tab and collect this major milestone.

tasks.title: See your full one hundred day stats
tasks.text: Open your stats and look across streak, money saved, cigarettes avoided, and health gains.

tasks.title: Write your one hundred day reflection
tasks.text: Write a few sentences on what one hundred days smoke free means to you.

tasks.title: Celebrate publicly
tasks.text: Share your one hundred day milestone with the community.

days.title: Day 101: Past the headline number
days.intro: The big round number is behind you. The work now is steady, quiet consistency.

tasks.title: Set a new personal target
tasks.text: Pick a new personal milestone to aim for, like a specific date or event.

tasks.title: Consistency beats big moments
tasks.text: Long term success comes from many ordinary days handled well, not from any single milestone, however big it feels.

days.title: Day 102: Stress resilience now
days.intro: Compare how you handle stress today to how you handled it on day five.

tasks.title: Compare stress responses
tasks.text: Write about how your reaction to a stressful moment today compares to early on in your quit.

tasks.title: Rate your stress resilience
tasks.text: Rate how well you currently handle stress without thinking of smoking.

days.title: Day 103: Fifteen weeks free
days.intro: Fifteen weeks. Over a third of the way to six months.

tasks.title: Claim your fifteen week badge
tasks.text: Open your badges tab and collect this milestone.

tasks.title: See your fifteen week stats
tasks.text: Open your stats and review your overall progress.

days.title: Day 104: Your new normal day
days.intro: Picture an average day now compared to an average day when you smoked.

tasks.title: Describe a normal day now
tasks.text: Write what a typical day looks like for you now, without any reference to smoking at all.

tasks.title: Notice what is missing
tasks.text: Notice that your description likely did not need to mention cigarettes at all, that absence is the real win.

days.title: Day 105: Confidence in hard rooms
days.intro: Being in a room full of smokers no longer has to feel like a test of strength.

tasks.title: Rate your comfort around smokers
tasks.text: Rate how comfortable you feel now being around people smoking, compared to month one.

tasks.title: Stay present in a smoking environment
tasks.text: If you are around smokers today, notice you can stay relaxed without needing to leave or react.

days.title: Day 106: What smoking used to cost you
days.intro: Beyond money, smoking had other costs, time, smell, health worry. Today is about naming those too.

tasks.title: List non money costs
tasks.text: Write down three things smoking used to cost you that were not about money, like time, smell, or constant worry.

tasks.title: See your total money saved
tasks.text: Open your money saved tab and look at the full total since day one.

days.title: Day 107: Sixteen weeks free
days.intro: Sixteen weeks. Four full months of consistency.

tasks.title: Claim your sixteen week badge
tasks.text: Open your badges tab and collect this milestone.

tasks.title: Share your four month update
tasks.text: Post a short update in the community about reaching four months.

days.title: Day 108: Reframing your past
days.intro: How you talk about your smoking past shapes how solid your non smoking present feels.

tasks.title: Write your past in one paragraph
tasks.text: Write a short paragraph about your smoking past as something that happened, not something that defines you.

tasks.title: Rate how you feel about your past self
tasks.text: Rate how much shame or judgment you still feel toward your past smoking self.

days.title: Day 109: Encouraging long term thinking
days.intro: It helps to occasionally picture yourself a year or more from now, still smoke free.

tasks.title: Picture one year from now
tasks.text: Write a few sentences imagining yourself one year from today, still smoke free.

tasks.title: Set a one year intention
tasks.text: Write one thing you want to be true about your life a year from now because you quit.

days.title: Day 110: Energy and mood
days.intro: Many people report steadier energy and mood by this stage compared to the rollercoaster of regular nicotine use.

tasks.title: Know the mood stability benefit
tasks.text: Without the rise and fall of nicotine levels throughout the day, many ex smokers experience steadier mood and energy rather than the dips smoking used to cause between cigarettes.

tasks.title: Rate your mood stability
tasks.text: Rate how stable your mood has felt this week.

days.title: Day 111: Seventeen weeks free
days.intro: Seventeen weeks. Getting close to chapter six and the second half of your guided plan.

tasks.title: Claim your seventeen week badge
tasks.text: Open your badges tab and collect this milestone.

tasks.title: See your seventeen week stats
tasks.text: Open your stats and review your full progress so far.

days.title: Day 112: Teaching what you know
days.intro: Explaining your own process to someone else often reveals how much you actually understand now.

tasks.title: Answer a question in the community
tasks.text: Find a question from a newer member and answer it with something specific that worked for you.

tasks.title: Explain your craving strategy
tasks.text: Write out, as if teaching someone else, exactly how you personally get through a craving now.

days.title: Day 113: Checking old triggers
days.intro: Revisit the original trigger list you made back in chapter one and see how much has changed.

tasks.title: Compare to your original triggers
tasks.text: Think back to the triggers you listed in chapter one and write about how much power each one still has over you now.

tasks.title: Rate your strongest remaining trigger
tasks.text: Rate the strength of whichever trigger still feels strongest today.

days.title: Day 114: Eighteen weeks free
days.intro: Eighteen weeks. Almost four and a half months in.

tasks.title: Claim your eighteen week badge
tasks.text: Open your badges tab and collect this milestone.

tasks.title: See your eighteen week numbers
tasks.text: Open your stats and review streak, money, and health progress.

days.title: Day 115: Non smoker, fully
days.intro: Today is simply about sitting with the fact that you are, plainly and fully, a non smoker now.

tasks.title: Write the plain fact
tasks.text: Write one simple sentence stating that you are a non smoker, without qualifiers or conditions.

tasks.title: Rate how true that feels
tasks.text: Rate how true that sentence feels to you right now.

days.title: Day 116: Health momentum
days.intro: Health improvements from quitting keep compounding well beyond the early months.

tasks.title: Know the long term momentum
tasks.text: Many health benefits from quitting continue to build for months and years, with risk reduction for several serious conditions increasing the longer you stay smoke free.

tasks.title: Do something for your future health
tasks.text: Do one thing today that supports your long term health, like a walk, water, or a good meal.

days.title: Day 117: Nineteen weeks free
days.intro: Nineteen weeks. One week away from chapter six.

tasks.title: Claim your nineteen week badge
tasks.text: Open your badges tab and collect this milestone.

tasks.title: Rate your overall chapter five experience
tasks.text: Rate how chapter five has felt for you overall.

days.title: Day 118: Preparing for hard days ahead
days.intro: Chapter six is about preparing for harder stretches, stress, slips, and tough seasons. Today is the bridge into it.

tasks.title: Know what chapter six covers
tasks.text: The next chapter focuses on preparing for genuinely hard days, including stress, possible slips, and tricky seasons like winter or holidays.

tasks.title: Think about your hardest season
tasks.text: Write about which time of year or type of situation you expect to be hardest for you going forward.

days.title: Day 119: One day before chapter six
days.intro: Tomorrow closes out a chapter focused on identity and confidence, and opens one about real world resilience.

tasks.title: Reflect on chapter five
tasks.text: Write a few sentences about how your sense of identity has shifted during this chapter.

tasks.title: Rate your confidence going into chapter six
tasks.text: Rate how prepared you feel for handling genuinely hard days ahead.

days.title: Day 120: Four months and a strong identity
days.intro: One hundred and twenty days. You are no longer someone trying to quit smoking, you are someone who quit. Chapter six prepares you for the days that test that the most.

tasks.title: See your four month transformation

tasks.text: Write a short summary of what changed in how you see yourself during this chapter.
